To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a Ca2+-independent, phorbol-myristate acetate-independent signaling pathway is involved in the stimulation of the respiratory response of neutrophil leukocytes.
the activation of the respiratory bursts by chemoattractant peptides does not involve an increase in [Ca2+], and that this activation is not inhibited by H7.
a receptor-mediated respiratory burst can be initiated in neutrophils that have been permeabilized electrically.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of calcium ions in the regulation of neutrophil function.
the mechanism by which neutrophils respond to chemotactic agents.
the role of Ca2+ in signal transduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the respiratory burst of neutrophils is mediated by three independent pathways.

fMLP induces a respiratory burst via a Ca2+-independent and protein kinase C-dependent pathway, whereas phorbol esters and diacylgycerol induce a respiratory burst via both Ca2+- and PKC-dependent pathways.
a receptor-mediated activation of electropermabilized neutrophil can be achieved in a Ca2+-and protein kinase C-independent pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found that the activation of neutrophils by chemoattractant receptors can be mediated by three distinct pathways: 1) activation of protein kinase A; 2) activation of protein kinases C and D, which require an increase in intracellular calcium; and 3) a pathway independent of protein kinase C or calcium.
the respiratory burst in neutrophils can be initiated by at least three distinct signaling pathways: changes in [Ca(2+)](i), protein kinase C activation, and an unknown pathway.
the respiratory burst is a result of the activation of protein kinase A, protein kinase C, and a third, unidentified kinase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a third signaling cascade, distinct from changes of intracellular free Ca(2+) and activation of protein C kinase C is involved in the neutrophil response to chemoattracts.
the respiratory burst is not mediated solely by changes in [Ca ^{2} ^{+} ] _{i}.
the respiratory burst can be activated by fMLP even in cells suspended in Ca2+-free medium.
